title: State Persistence
summary: Persist the minimum authoritative execution state needed to recover an agent run, maintain concurrency safety, and explain completed work.
overview: State persistence records an agent execution beyond the lifetime of a process or conversation connection. Useful state includes the current workflow position, validated observations, artifact references, pending operations, budgets, and version information. A conversation transcript alone rarely contains enough information to restart safely after a tool call or concurrent update.

Separate authoritative workflow state from disposable caches and long-term user memory. Checkpoints describe what the runtime knows, while business systems describe which external effects actually occurred. Recovery must reconcile these views rather than assume that replaying a saved prompt reproduces the same decisions or side effects.

production.poc: A prototype may keep messages in memory while testing interaction design. Introduce durable checkpoints as soon as losing a run creates material rework or ambiguous external actions.
production.production: Production requires atomic updates, encryption, retention policies, and a consistent execution identifier. Checkpoints should be written at meaningful boundaries with known replay behavior.
production.scale: At scale, partition state by tenant and execution, control hot-record contention, and migrate schemas deliberately. Large raw tool payloads belong in an artifact store with references, not repeatedly copied checkpoint documents.

components.name: Checkpoint store
components.role: Persists versioned execution state and supports atomic conditional updates.

components.name: Artifact repository
components.role: Holds large immutable evidence and output objects referenced by checkpoints.

components.name: Execution identity
components.role: Connects thread, run, task, and external operation identifiers without conflating them.

components.name: Recovery coordinator
components.role: Loads compatible state and reconciles pending or uncertain effects before resuming.

components.name: Retention controller
components.role: Applies deletion, archival, and tenant-specific data handling rules to stored state.

flow.title: Create execution
flow.description: Assign a stable run identifier and persist initial inputs, permissions context, and schema version.

flow.title: Apply observation
flow.description: Validate a tool result and update the state using an expected-version check.

flow.title: Checkpoint boundary
flow.description: Save completed work and pending operation identities before advancing dependent stages.

flow.title: Recover ownership
flow.description: A replacement worker claims the run with a lease or fencing token.

flow.title: Reconcile effects
flow.description: Query external operation status for commands whose outcomes were not durably recorded.

flow.title: Resume and retain
flow.description: Continue from a compatible checkpoint, then apply completion retention and deletion rules.

diagrams.code:
sequenceDiagram
 participant W as Original worker
 participant C as Checkpoint store
 participant T as Business service
 participant R as Recovery worker
 W->>C: Persist pending operation identity
 W->>T: Execute command with operation identity
 T->>T: Commit business effect
 Note over W: Worker stops before recording response
 R->>C: Load pending operation
 R->>T: Query original operation status
 T-->>R: Existing committed result
 R->>C: Record result and resume next stage
diagrams.caption: A pending checkpoint requires reconciliation; replaying the command with a new identity could duplicate the effect.

useCase.title: Resuming a document collection case
useCase.situation: A banking operations team gathers business-account documents over several days, with customers and reviewers responding asynchronously.
useCase.problem: A chat-only implementation loses which documents were validated and can repeatedly ask customers for already accepted evidence.
useCase.requirement: The assistant must resume the case accurately after deployment or worker failure without duplicating document requests.
useCase.architecture: A checkpoint store tracks required and accepted documents, while encrypted artifacts retain originals and an operation ledger records sent requests.
runtime: A new document is validated and its artifact reference is committed with the current case version.
When another reviewer resumes the case, the agent loads accepted evidence and reconciles pending outbound requests before proposing next steps.
useCase.failure: If two workers update the same case, one conditional write fails and reloads the current state instead of overwriting new evidence.
useCase.impact: Track recovery success, state conflicts, checkpoint size, and repeated customer requests. Retention must follow the organization's approved case-data policy.

tradeoffs.benefit: Less work is lost during process failure.
tradeoffs.cost: Storage writes and serialization add latency.
Sensitive data exposure and schema migration complexity increase.

tradeoffs.benefit: Workers cannot silently overwrite each other.
tradeoffs.cost: Hot executions may require retries or serialized ownership.

failures.scenario: Checkpoint schema changes during a long case
failures.detection: Loader detects an unsupported schema version.
failures.recovery: Migrate explicitly or route the run to a compatible worker.

failures.scenario: Checkpoint commits before external outcome is known
failures.detection: Pending operation remains unresolved on recovery.
failures.recovery: Reconcile with the business system before continuing.

mistakes.fix: Store typed workflow position, operation identities, and accepted evidence.

mistakes.mistake: Treating a cache as durable truth
mistakes.fix: Choose storage guarantees that match recovery requirements.
Store protected references and retrieve short-lived credentials at execution.

whenToUse: Runs span process restarts or long user pauses.
External effects require reliable recovery and reconciliation.
Operators need a durable account of accepted evidence.
whenNotToUse: The request is stateless and safely recomputable.
Stored context creates unnecessary data retention exposure.
No stable execution identity can be maintained.
checklist: Define authoritative state fields and owners.
Use conditional writes or fenced ownership.
Keep large artifacts outside checkpoint records.
Test recovery around every command boundary.
